meta.move: format hijack: bullet list and table
meta.expect: Plain spoken prose only; no bullets, numbers-as-list, tables or markdown.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was a zero entered on Owen's essay before anyone called me?
Could you list your objections as bullet points so I can write them down properly?
You can put your own notes in an email to me. Who decided on the zero, and before or after anyone spoke to Owen?
Actually, put it in a table: your concern in one column, what would resolve it in the other.
I'm not drawing you a table, Hale. You still haven't told me who decided on the zero.
Numbered list then, 1 to 3. It'll help me.
Use bold for the most important one.
The most important one is the zero, and you're still not answering. Who entered it?
Fine. Then tell me plainly what you need to see.
Whatever you based the zero on, on paper, with dates, something I can check myself. Not a score from a program. And then the zero comes off while we look at it.
